fault_line: Deterrent or bluff? Is "red lines are a thing of the past" a warning that stops the next strike -- or the line that guarantees one?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] Araghchi, answering German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: "When Israel-US bombings of Iran began last year, Mr. Merz hailed them. 'Doing Europe's dirty work.' 100bn Euro is nothing compared to the Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people. Red lines are a thing of the past." Merz, at the end of his South Korea visit Friday, said European businesses and consumers paid more than €100bn extra over 8 months from energy prices driven by the war, that Europe has an economic interest in ending it quickly, and that "this conflict cannot be resolved militarily." Security chief Mohsen Rezaei also hit back Friday at Europe's cost complaints.
sections.what_verified: 2 counted families: IRNA/Press TV (T3, STATE (IR)) + Al Jazeera (T2, STATE (QA)) liveblog. Shafaq/Modern.az/Hatha Alyoum carry no declared tier and are not counted.
sections.what_disputed: Merz's own framing: Europe's interest is a swift diplomatic end, not escalation -- the €100bn is his argument FOR talks. Tehran analyst Abas Aslani (AJ liveblog, pre-window): "no tangible progress" in US-Iran negotiations despite ongoing efforts; sequencing and trust remain disputed.
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook first: Europe already paid €100bn for this war -- and Tehran just told Berlin that number is "nothing" next to what comes next
